title: SQL Injection
subject: cybersecurity
description: Understand how SQL injection works, recognize vulnerable queries, and practice preventing the attack.

steps.title: What is SQL Injection?
steps.content: SQL injection happens when untrusted user input is directly combined with a database query. An attacker can manipulate that input to change what the database executes.

steps.title: See the Attack
steps.content: Imagine a login query that combines a username directly into SQL. If the input changes the structure of the query, the attacker may bypass the intended login logic.

steps.title: Identify the Vulnerability
steps.question: Which practice creates the highest SQL injection risk?
steps.options: ["Parameterized queries", "Directly concatenating user input into SQL", "Using prepared statements", "Validating input"]
steps.answer: Directly concatenating user input into SQL

steps.title: Fix the Query
steps.content: Modify the vulnerable query so that user input is handled safely.
steps.starter_code: query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = '" + username + "'"
steps.expected_output: Use a parameterized query instead of string concatenation.

steps.title: Choose the Defense
steps.question: Which technique is commonly used to prevent SQL injection?

steps.title: Apply the Defense
steps.content: You are reviewing an API that accepts a username. Describe how you would safely pass that username to a database query.
steps.starter_code: query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = '" + username + "'"
steps.expected_output: Replace string concatenation with a parameterized query or prepared statement.

title: Authentication vs Authorization
subject: cybersecurity
description: Learn the difference between proving who you are and determining what you are allowed to access.

steps.title: Authentication
steps.content: Authentication answers: Who are you? Logging in with a password, passkey, or other identity mechanism is authentication.

steps.title: Authorization
steps.content: Authorization answers: What are you allowed to do? A logged-in user may still be blocked from accessing an administrator-only resource.

steps.title: Pick the Status Code
steps.question: A user is logged in but does not have permission to access /admin. Which status code is appropriate?

steps.title: Find the Missing Control
steps.content: A normal user can access GET /admin/users after successfully logging in. What should the backend check before returning the data?
steps.expected_output: Add an authorization or role check before returning administrator data.

steps.title: Authentication or Authorization?
steps.question: Checking whether a user has the admin role is an example of what?

steps.title: Secure the Endpoint
steps.content: Modify the endpoint logic so only administrators can access administrator data.
steps.expected_output: Check the user's role or permission before returning admin_users.

title: Python Functions
subject: python
description: Understand functions, return values, and how to modify a simple Python function.

steps.title: What is a Function?
steps.content: A function is a reusable block of code designed to perform a particular task. It can receive inputs and return an output.

steps.title: Return Values
steps.content: The return statement sends a value back to the code that called the function. Returning a value is different from simply printing it.

steps.title: Choose the Keyword
steps.question: Which keyword sends a value back from a Python function?

steps.title: Fix the Function
steps.content: Modify the function so it returns the sum instead of printing it.
steps.expected_output: def add(a, b):\n    return a + b

steps.title: Predict the Result
steps.question: What does add(2, 3) return if the function uses return a + b?

steps.title: Create a Greeting Function
steps.content: Write a function that accepts a name and returns a greeting.
steps.starter_code: def greet(name):\n    # write your code here
steps.expected_output: The function should return a greeting containing the provided name.

title: Binary Search
subject: dsa
description: Understand how binary search reduces the search space and practice implementing its core logic.

steps.title: The Search Space
steps.content: Binary search works on sorted data. Instead of checking every element, it repeatedly divides the remaining search space in half.

steps.title: Why O(log n)?
steps.content: Each comparison removes roughly half of the remaining elements. This produces logarithmic time complexity: O(log n).

steps.title: Time Complexity
steps.question: What is the average time complexity of binary search on a sorted array?

steps.title: Choose the Middle
steps.content: Complete the missing line used to calculate the middle index.

steps.title: When Can You Use It?
steps.question: What condition is required for standard binary search?
steps.options: ["The data must be sorted", "The data must contain strings", "The array must have 10 elements", "The data must be random"]

steps.title: Fix the Search
steps.content: Complete the condition that moves the search to the left half when the target is smaller than the middle element.

title: Phishing Detection
subject: cybersecurity
description: Learn to identify phishing indicators and practice analyzing suspicious messages.

steps.title: What is Phishing?
steps.content: Phishing is a social engineering technique where attackers impersonate trusted entities to trick people into revealing information or taking unsafe actions.

steps.title: Spot the Red Flags
steps.content: Common indicators include urgent requests, suspicious links, unexpected attachments, credential requests, unusual domains, and pressure to act immediately.

steps.title: Find the Strongest Signal
steps.question: Which is a strong phishing indicator?
steps.options: ["A normal greeting", "An urgent request for credentials", "A known company logo", "A familiar email signature"]

steps.title: Inspect the Link
steps.content: You receive a message asking you to log in immediately. The displayed link says example.com but points to a different domain. What should you do?
steps.expected_output: Treat the mismatch as suspicious and do not enter credentials.

steps.title: What Should You Verify?
steps.question: Before entering credentials from an unexpected message, what should you verify?
steps.options: ["Only the logo", "The actual destination and sender", "The message font", "The email length"]

steps.title: Write the Safe Action
steps.content: Write the safest response to a suspicious message requesting immediate password verification.
steps.expected_output: Do not use the message link. Verify through an official channel or website.

title: REST API Fundamentals
subject: web_development
description: Understand REST APIs and practice designing a simple endpoint.

steps.title: What is an API?
steps.content: An API defines how software components communicate. A web API lets a client send requests to a server and receive structured responses.

steps.title: HTTP Methods
steps.content: GET commonly retrieves data, POST creates data, PUT replaces a resource, PATCH partially updates it, and DELETE removes it.

steps.title: Choose the Method
steps.question: Which HTTP method is commonly used to partially update a resource?

steps.title: Design an Endpoint
steps.content: Design an endpoint that returns a user's profile as JSON.
steps.expected_output: Return a structured JSON object containing the user's profile information.

steps.title: API Response Format
steps.question: Which format is commonly used for REST API responses?

steps.title: Create a Response
steps.content: Create a simple JSON response containing a user's name and skill.
steps.expected_output: A JSON object containing fields such as name and skill.
